_notes: Broadcast destination requirements as data, not code. Adding a landscape
platform is an entry here; adding a vertical one is an entry plus a second
encode, which is why the card renderer keeps a 9:16 layout in its design.
Refresh cadence: review at each release, and whenever a platform announces
an ingest change. The fields that actually gate a stream are ingest_url,
requires_cbr and keyframe_secs; the rest is guidance surfaced in the UI.
V1 ships Twitch and YouTube only: both take a persistent key with no
account gating and both accept landscape 720p. Everything under 'deferred'
is documented with the reason it is not in v1.

audio._note: AAC everywhere. No platform accepts Opus on ingest, so the broadcast leg transcodes even though the session speaks Opus end to end.

platforms.key_acquisition: Creator Dashboard, Settings, Stream, Primary Stream key. Persistent until reset.
platforms.notes: Twitch requires constant bitrate; variable bitrate shows up as viewer buffering rather than an ingest error. The regional ingest list is served over their API, but live.twitch.tv resolves to a nearby POP and is what the docs recommend for a fixed configuration.

platforms.key_acquisition: YouTube Studio, Go Live, Stream, Stream key. Persistent keys are the default; the channel needs live streaming enabled once, which can take 24 hours on a new account.
platforms.notes: YouTube enforces a 4 s maximum keyframe interval and recommends 2 s. Sending 2 s satisfies both platforms with one encode.

deferred.reason: Ingest keys are per-broadcast and minted through the Graph API, so a session cannot be configured ahead of time with a persistent key. Needs an OAuth app review.
No public RTMP ingest for ordinary accounts; vertical only, so it also needs the second encode.
RTMP ingest is gated behind follower thresholds and a per-region application. Vertical, so it needs the second encode.
Persistent key and landscape, so technically the cheapest addition; deferred only to keep v1 to the two platforms we can test end to end.
